name: LTC3260EMSE#TRPBF
title: LTC3260: low noise dual supply inverting charge pump, 4.5V to 32V input
summary: The LTC3260 makes a positive and a negative low-noise rail from one 4.5V to 32V supply. An inverting charge pump delivers up to 100mA at about –VIN, and two adjustable LDOs, a negative one fed from the pump and a positive one fed from VIN, each supply up to 50mA. The pump runs either at constant frequency, set between 50kHz and 500kHz by one resistor, for low noise, or in Burst Mode operation near –0.94 • VIN, where the part draws 100µA with both LDOs on. Short-circuit limiting and thermal shutdown are built in; packages are a 14-lead 4mm × 3mm DFN and a 16-lead MSOP, both with an exposed ground pad.
key_figures: –VIN (constant frequency) or –0.94 • VIN (Burst Mode operation), up to 100mA
100µA typ in Burst Mode operation with both LDOs on; 2µA typ in shutdown
50kHz to 500kHz by RT; 500kHz typ with RT = GND

notes: All finishes are lead free. The temperature grade (E, I, H, MP) is shown on a label on the shipping container, not in the marking.
Temperature range is the operating junction range; the grades differ in how far their limits are guaranteed (Note 2).

circuits.title: ±12V outputs from a single 15V input
circuits.description: A 15V supply becomes +12V and –12V low-noise rails. EN+ and EN– are tied to the input so both regulators run whenever power is present, and MODE is grounded so the charge pump runs at constant frequency, set to 200kHz by the 200k resistor on RT. The pump, with a 1µF flying capacitor, makes about –15V on VOUT; the positive LDO runs from the input and the negative LDO from VOUT. Each output is set by a 909k over 100k divider into its ADJ pin, and 10nF on each BYP pin quiets the references.

circuits.title: Low power ±24V supply from a single-ended 28V input
circuits.description: A 28V input gives +24V and –24V at low quiescent current. MODE is tied high to the input with both enables, so the charge pump runs in Burst Mode operation; RT is grounded for the 500kHz rate. 1.91M over 100k dividers set the two LDO outputs. The reference bypass pins are left open, and all supply, pump and output capacitors are 4.7µF except the 1µF flying capacitor.
notes: Pin numbers follow the 14-lead DFN.

circuits.title: High voltage input to bipolar output with a dividing/inverting charge pump
circuits.description: From 13.5V to 32V in, the part makes +5V and –5V. Two pump capacitors (C2, C3) and three MBR0540 Schottky diodes around C+ and C– turn the inverter into a divide-by-two inverter, so VOUT sits near minus half the input. Because VOUT is always below –½VIN the pump stays in constant frequency operation whatever MODE is set to; in this circuit MODE, RT and GND all go to ground. 316k over 100k dividers set the outputs and 0.01µF capacitors bypass both references.
notes: Pin numbers are those of the 16-lead MSOP.
VOUT ≈ –((VIN – VF – |IOUT| • ROL) / 2 – VF), VF being the Schottky forward drop.

circuits.title: 28V dual tracking bipolar supply with outputs from ±5V to ±25V
circuits.description: One chain of resistors runs from LDO+ to LDO– with no tap to ground: R1 from LDO+ to ADJ+, R2 and the 500k variable resistor R3 from ADJ+ to ADJ–, and R4 from ADJ– to LDO–. Turning R3 moves both outputs together, from ±5V to ±25V, so the negative rail tracks the positive one. MODE and RT are grounded for 500kHz constant frequency operation from a 28V input, and 0.01µF capacitors bypass both references.

circuits.title: Positive LDO application circuit
circuits.description: The positive LDO alone: LDO+ drives the output, R1 and R2 divide it down into ADJ+, COUT holds the output steady, and an optional CBYP+ from BYP+ to ground bypasses the 1.2V reference. EN+ switches the regulator on and off; it is powered from VIN.
notes: Only the pins of the positive regulator take part.

circuits.title: Negative LDO application circuit
circuits.description: The negative LDO alone, fed inside the part from the charge pump output VOUT. R1 from LDO– to ADJ– and R2 from ADJ– to ground set the output; COUT holds it steady, CBYP– bypasses the –1.2V reference, and CADJ– across R1 speeds the transient response. EN– enables the pump and this regulator together.
notes: Only the pins of the negative regulator take part; VOUT has no outside connection in this circuit.

operation.text: One positive input of 4.5V to 32V makes a bipolar pair of quiet rails: an inverting charge pump produces a negative supply on VOUT, a negative LDO runs from VOUT, and an independent positive LDO runs from VIN.
With both EN+ and EN– low everything but the internal bias is off, and the part takes 2µA typ from VIN.

MODE low selects it; EN– turns on the pump and oscillator. In the first half of each clock, S1 and S2 close and the flying capacitor between C+ and C– charges to VIN. In the second half S1 and S2 open and S3 and S4 close: C+ goes to ground and charge flows out of C– into VOUT. In steady state VOUT settles at –VIN minus the drop caused by the load on VOUT and on the negative LDO.
A resistor on RT sets the charge transfer rate from 50kHz to 500kHz; RT grounded gives 500kHz. At lower frequency the pump's ROL is higher and it can supply less average current.

MODE high selects it. The pump charges VOUT to –0.94 • VIN typ, then stops the oscillator and sleeps, drawing about 100µA with both LDOs on. When VOUT has drooped by the comparator hysteresis the part wakes and pumps until VOUT passes –0.94 • VIN again. Supply current is lower but output ripple is higher, which suits light loads. RT sets the rate of the charge cycles; grounding RT is recommended, as it gives the lowest ROL, the fastest charge to the burst threshold and the longest sleep.

Internal circuitry ramps up the current available to the output capacitor slowly to limit start-up current. A commanded shutdown or a thermal shutdown resets it. The pump's soft-start also limits inrush for the negative LDO, whose input VOUT is at GND until EN– goes high. The positive LDO has its own soft-start that brings its target voltage up from 0 to full scale over 75µs, easing inrush on VIN.

In a short the output current is limited to about 160mA. Above roughly 175°C junction temperature, thermal shutdown stops current delivery to the output; it resumes when the junction cools to roughly 165°C. The protection is for brief overloads: the junction is then outside its operating range, and continuous operation above the maximum operating junction temperature can harm reliability.

Takes power from VIN and supplies up to 50mA. A divider from LDO+ through ADJ+ to GND sets the output. The output needs a low-ESR ceramic capacitor that keeps at least 2µF over temperature and bias. EN+ turns it on and off. An optional 10nF from BYP+ to ground bypasses the internal 1.2V reference and lowers noise; unused, BYP+ stays open.

Takes power from VOUT and supplies up to 50mA. A divider from LDO– through ADJ– to GND sets the output, which needs a low-ESR ceramic capacitor keeping at least 2µF over temperature and bias. EN– turns it on with the charge pump. An optional 10nF from BYP– to ground bypasses the –1.2V reference and lowers noise; unused, BYP– stays open. A capacitor CADJ– across the upper divider resistor, 10pF recommended and 2pF to 22pF worth trying, improves transient response.

operation.topic: Negative LDO headroom in Burst Mode operation
operation.text: With the pump in Burst Mode operation the hysteresis on VOUT is typically 2% of VIN. Set LDO– far enough above VOUT that the regulator stays out of dropout in normal operation.

ROL measures how strong the charge pump is. It depends on the oscillator frequency, the flying capacitor value, the non-overlap time, the internal switch resistances and the ESR of the external capacitors. At 500kHz it rises with temperature, typically from 24Ω to 28Ω at –50°C to about 50Ω to 54Ω at 150°C.

The capacitors decide loop stability, output ripple, pump strength and minimum turn-on time. Low-ESR ceramics are recommended on the charge pump and LDO outputs, each keeping at least 2µF over temperature and bias. Tantalum or aluminium parts may be added in parallel for more capacitance but not used alone, because of their ESR. In constant frequency mode COUT sets the output ripple for a given load; a larger COUT lowers ripple but lengthens the minimum turn-on time. CIN sets the ripple on VIN and how much is needed depends on the source impedance; VIN should see 2µF or more of low-ESR capacitance, with a ceramic as the main bypass and tantalum or aluminium in parallel if wanted.

For the full rated pump output current use a ceramic flying capacitor of 1µF or more. Very light loads can use less: 0.2µF may do for up to 20mA. A smaller flying capacitor raises ROL and so lowers the maximum load current.

X5R and X7R dielectrics hold most of their capacitance from –40°C to 85°C; Z5U and Y5V lose a great deal over that span and can lose 60% or more at rated voltage. Compare parts by the capacitance actually achieved in a given case size, and confirm from the capacitor's own data that the capacitance holds at the working temperature and voltage.

Switching frequency and transient currents are high, so use a true ground plane and short connections to every external capacitor. C+ and C– carry large fast currents; keep them away from ADJ+, ADJ–, BYP+ and BYP–.

At high input voltage and full load the dissipation can be large; above about 175°C junction the output is shut off. A good thermal path to the ground plane, with the exposed pad tied to ground copper on two board layers under the part, lowers the thermal resistance considerably. The maximum dissipation falls linearly with ambient temperature, from about 4.65W at –50°C to zero at 150°C. The 43°C/W θJA it assumes is reached on a four-layer board with 2oz copper, the exposed pad joined to the ground plane by six vias. Continuous operation should stay at TJ ≤ 150°C; beyond that performance and life can suffer. Thermal shutdown disables all outputs at about 175°C typ and re-enables them at about 165°C.
